aggressive_definition: High-grade prostate cancer, defined in the abstract as Gleason score greater than 7.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: Multivariable logistic regression was used to calculate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the associations between alcohol intake and low-grade (Gleason <7) and high-grade (Gleason >7) PCa.
study_design: Secondary risk-factor analysis of a 4-year multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with baseline alcohol assessment and protocol biopsies at 2 and 4 years.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: Of 6374 participants in our analysis, approximately 25% reported no alcohol consumption, 49% were moderate drinkers (one to seven drinks per week), and 26% were heavy drinkers (more than seven drinks per week).
reason: Participants had a recent negative prostate biopsy and underwent follow-up biopsies, establishing incident ascertainment. The abstract analyzes low-grade and high-grade disease but does not report a total/general prostate cancer analysis. The high-grade case count is supplied by existing full-text evidence.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: In contrast, men randomized to dutasteride and reporting more than seven drinks per week were 86% more likely to be diagnosed with high-grade PCa (p=0.01).
estimate_classifications.reason: The row compares heavy alcohol intake with abstention among dutasteride-treated men for incident high-grade prostate cancer; its exact OR and CI are provided by the supplied full-text evidence.
